text: Ephrata Recovery & Capacity Plan
Completed operating playbook · September 8, 2026 decision snapshot · September 8–21 operating window

Submission deadline: October 11, 2026, 3:00 PM PDT. The simulation produces a plan for ten business days; no live repair, customer message, cancellation action, or restart has been performed. The case and complete source context are in the first tab. This completed playbook follows the original eleven-step framework and incorporates the user-approved 47-hour Ephrata allocation.
Step 1: Define the problem and desired outcome

Senior Helpers Ephrata purchased automatic shift-end availability, routing to current on-call staff, and relief from morning dashboard checks. Carol Ann Frees reports that both availability and routing failures have recurred despite ticket closures and a connected WellSky account. The desired outcome is a reliable workflow that removes required manual corrections and gives her confidence to stop routine checking.

The portfolio problem is equally concrete: one five-person team must investigate Ephrata, complete Durant's agreed September 18 cancellation obligations, and answer Medford's overdue restart request before its September 22 board review. Success is a defensible allocation, verified evidence where available, and explicit decisions on work that cannot fit.
Step 2: Organize the evidence

Recorded facts: August 11 engineering checked a valid token and one afternoon manual re-sync, which changed Denise's status in about 90 seconds. August 13 configuration replaced an April rotation with a June 30 roster. An August 14 test at 11:20 a.m. reached Denise. The outcome ticket closed August 18 pending customer confirmation, and the account was marked green August 21. These establish narrow checks and internal closure, not overnight reliability.

Customer reports: August 24 brought two good mornings with a request to observe longer. On September 8, Carol Ann reported correcting two caregivers on three mornings the previous week and another weekend call reaching her instead of Marcus. HS-48251 is open and high priority but not yet triaged to engineering in the supplied record.

The August 25 adoption snapshot shows 11 of 14 caregivers consistently confirming shift end and three admin-closeout patterns. Those three have not been matched to the September complaint. Inference: outcome verification and workflow ownership were inadequate. Unknowns: current technical cause, intended automatic trigger, current approved roster, actual call trace, failure denominator, and minutes of required manual work. The diagnosis memo contains the complete dated evidence map.
Step 3: Map the current workflow

Availability: shift end → intended app or scheduled event → Casey job → caregiver mapping and WellSky write → persisted unavailable status → morning dashboard. First establish which trigger is intended; then distinguish a missing event, a rejected write, a wrong record, and a value that did not persist.

Routing: approved roster with effective dates → maintained Riley configuration → after-hours and rotation rules → intended recipient → acknowledgment or approved fallback. The June roster is historical evidence and must not be assumed to be September's authoritative rotation.

Outcome ownership: technical evidence → exception owner → customer verification → closure. Priya owns the recovery outcome, Nate technical evidence, Diego business-hours evidence collection, Jordan peer review, and the Head capacity and escalation. Confirm the customer's roster maintainer and receiving owner on Day 1; those assignments are not supplied facts.
Step 4: Diagnose the underlying constraint

The strongest supported diagnosis is that ticket closure and connection health were treated as proof of customer relief. The technical cause of the recurrence remains unresolved. Investigate stale roster/effective-time rules, missing shift-end events or adoption, and mapping/permission/job/retry/persistence problems as separate hypotheses. Caregiver retraining alone cannot explain the routing failure.

Engineering is the scarce skill. Routing review requires an estimated 3–6 hours and the WellSky audit 6–10 hours. Together they consume 9–16 hours before separately sized remediation. The authorized Ephrata ceiling is nine hours. The plan deliberately funds the lower bounds and accepts that diagnosis or partial containment may be the outcome.
Step 5: Resolve consequential uncertainty

Day 1: obtain affected caregiver IDs and shift-end times, the weekend call timestamp, current approved roster, system access, authorized test recipients, and a manual-work baseline. Confirm the team's individual calendars and the proposed 36/25-hour strategist split. Missing evidence becomes a named blocker, not an assumed answer.

Days 2–4: trace routing first, then affected availability cases alongside a matched successful case. Capture expected versus actual state, event/write timestamps, recipient/fallback, and evidence references. Establish an appropriate latency bound with Carol Ann and Nate before scoring availability tests; the historical 90-second manual result is not an agreed SLA.

Stop rule: after each Nate block, log consumed hours and forecast remaining work. At a forecast above nine hours, or when correction plus retest cannot fit, stop additional engineering work and have the Head request a sized allocation decision from the engineering authority. Keep the recovery open.
Step 6: Choose the smallest meaningful intervention

Use bounded routing review, an end-to-end WellSky audit, targeted adoption outreach, explicit exception ownership, and a customer outcome gate. A reversible configuration correction is conditional on evidence, authority, and correction plus retest fitting the same nine-hour envelope. A broad rebuild or new automation is deferred until sized and approved.

Durant gets a validated export, final invoice reconciliation through September 18, and deactivation on its agreed final service day. Medford gets an overdue reply, a reset conversation, and a scoped proposal with prerequisites and approvals. The proposal does not promise a production restart.
Step 7: Allocate resources and sequence work
Decision and capacity envelope

Ephrata: 47 hours — Head 4; Priya 20; Jordan 4; Diego 10; Nate 9. Durant: 10 hours — Head 1; Jordan 5; Diego 4. Medford: 5 hours — Head 1; Jordan 4. Shared portfolio coordination: 5.5 hours — Head 0.5; Priya 3; Jordan 2. Protected support queue coverage: 14 Diego hours.

Person ceilings and planned use: Head 6.5 of 7.5 hours; Priya 23 of proposed 36; Jordan 15 of proposed 25; Diego 28 of 34 including 14 queue hours; Nate 9 of 24 across the wider account book. The only sourced strategist limit is 61 combined hours, so the 36/25 split requires Day 1 confirmation. Daily availability profiles are proposed calendars, not additional sourced capacity.

Planned work and coverage total 81.5 hours. Leave 30 nonengineering hours unallocated: Head 1, Priya 13, Jordan 10, Diego 6. Nate's remaining 15 hours are preserved for the wider account book and are not discretionary Ephrata reserve. No account receives extra hours until a named owner/date is added and the workbook checks pass.

Efficiency decision approved by the user: Diego retains five hours for daily observation evidence collection; Priya reviews the five-day sample in six hours, rather than fourteen. Use two Priya hours on September 14 and one on September 15–18. Keep all acceptance criteria, peer review, and leadership gates. This frees eight strategist hours for exceptions instead of duplicating collection and review.

Protect Durant's nine strategist/CSM hours, the upper estimate for offboarding, plus one leadership hour. Protect Medford's four strategist hours, the upper estimate for scoping/proposal, plus one leadership hour. An additional Ephrata engineer would consume capacity preserved for other accounts and require approval; unused strategist hours cannot substitute for that skill.
Ten-business-day execution sequence

Day 1 · Sep 8: Priya triages and assembles the incident packet; Diego pulls adoption evidence; the Head confirms limits. Jordan starts Durant export preparation, answers Tom's missed follow-up, and confirms calendars. These are proposed actions, not messages already sent.

Day 2 · Sep 9: Nate spends three hours on routing configuration and agreed controlled tests; Priya prepares current-roster cases; Diego conducts targeted caregiver outreach. Jordan generates Durant's export; Diego independently validates it. Jordan also prepares and conducts Medford's 30-minute reset conversation, subject to Tom's availability.

Day 3 · Sep 10: Nate begins the WellSky trace in a three-hour block; Priya maps failed shift-end cases; Jordan peer-reviews the test design. Diego establishes exception tracking and validates Durant's drafted final invoice. Jordan resolves export format and validation issues.

Day 4 · Sep 11: Nate finishes the six-hour WellSky audit within the total nine-hour cap. Priya holds the proposed verification conversation and written follow-up. The Head records Ready for observation, Inconclusive, or Blocked. Jordan targets delivery of the validated Durant export; Diego confirms receipt. September 11 remains the documented export target, not a new guarantee.

Day 5 · Sep 14: Diego collects morning sample 1 and weekend evidence; Priya reviews it retrospectively in two hours. There is no added staffed weekend or overnight shift. Jordan drafts Medford's scoped proposal; the Head reviews its authority boundaries.

Day 6 · Sep 15: Diego collects morning sample 2; Priya reviews it in one hour; Jordan peer-reviews interpretation. The Head assesses exceptions and whether additional authorized nonengineering reserve should be scheduled.

Day 7 · Sep 16: Diego collects morning sample 3; Priya reviews it in one hour and checks reserve/queue separation. Jordan reviews receiving-owner readiness. The Head confirms Durant's final-service-day readiness using actual export receipt and invoice evidence.
Day 8 · Sep 17: Diego collects morning sample 4; Priya reviews it in one hour and checks rotation exposure. The Head reviews remaining acceptance gaps; Jordan reconciles the three-account sequence.

Day 9 · Sep 18: Diego collects morning sample 5; Priya reviews it in one hour and prepares the acceptance packet. Diego executes Durant's documented WellSky/Riley/Casey deactivation on the agreed final service day; Jordan and the Head confirm invoice/service closure or log an exception. Confirm the authorized cutoff before deactivation so service is not ended early.

Day 10 · Sep 21: Priya reviews outcomes with Carol Ann; Diego demonstrates evidence retrieval and exception intake; Jordan observes the receiving-owner demonstration; the Head decides the recovery status. Jordan finalizes Medford's board-ready proposal and the Head reviews outstanding approvals. Customer unavailability is recorded as a gap, not acceptance.

Diego's 14 queue hours are scheduled separately across all ten days. The workbook contains 69 individual work records, every person/day allocation, and proposed daily limits. If a prerequisite fails, repurpose only explicitly reassigned hours within the actual ceiling; do not count a blocked task as completed.
Deferrals, consequences, and authority

Deferred: extra Ephrata engineering or broad custom automation; consequence: recovery may remain unresolved. Head escalates a sized request. Deferred: Medford production restart and commercial changes; consequence: the board receives a proposal and dependencies, not a live pilot or launch date. Jordan scopes and the Head routes approvals.

Deferred: durable Ephrata acceptance if the representative sample is incomplete or a recurrence resets it; consequence: recovery remains open and later observation must be resourced. Priya owns the open gate. Staffing changes, other-account load changes, new fix-by dates or service promises, credits, changed Durant final date, and unapproved Medford pricing/term/scope changes require the relevant authority through the Head.
Step 8: Build or implement the working intervention

Built for the simulation: ephrata_diagnosis.md, ten_day_operating_plan.xlsx, and ephrata_handoff.md. The workbook's Capacity, Daily plan, Work log, and Inputs tabs connect editable inputs to live allocation, daily conflicts, protected coverage, calendar/milestone, and evidence checks. The handoff sequences six Ephrata stages with owners, prerequisites, hours, next actions, unsent customer drafts, and stop rules.

Proposed for real execution: set HS-48251 as the parent recovery record linking the three August tickets. Maintain separate availability, routing, adoption, and customer-outcome workstreams. Every blocked item records owner, blocker, next step, next checkpoint, hours used, and approval needed. Planned/Blocked/Done status must reflect actual evidence; Done without evidence is flagged in the workbook.
Step 9: Test behavior and verify value

Proposed implementation gate: approved current roster, trigger, mappings, permissions, exception path, and any actual correction are documented with before/after evidence and rollback. Proposed operation gate: trace affected and representative compliant caregivers to persisted status; test after-hours, rotation-boundary, and agreed no-answer/missing-data paths; record expected/actual results and denominators.

Proposed user-outcome gate, conditional on readiness by September 11: sample five business mornings September 14–18 and retrospectively review September 12–13 evidence. Aim for zero required availability corrections, zero unexplained misroutes in eligible observed calls, and Carol Ann's confirmation that routine verification is no longer necessary. Compare minutes of required manual work with the Day 1 baseline. These criteria are proposals to agree, not contractual SLAs or observed results.

Zero eligible calls does not establish natural routing success. Controlled tests alone do not prove sustained relief. A later correction resets the relevant observation sample and may push acceptance beyond the window. Missing access, latency criteria, representative cases, or customer acceptance is reported explicitly as Inconclusive or Blocked.

Actual artifact validation: twelve meaningful input-change tests passed, including engineering overage, coverage shortfall, person/day capacity reduction, missing evidence, blocked-without-next-step, missing capacity, calendar/date changes, duplicate dates, and unauthorized source-capacity increases. Recalculation found no formula errors, and XLSX export/reimport preserved the base allocation and checks. Rendered views from all four tabs were reviewed. Excel desktop was not opened; customer workflows remain untested in this simulation.
Step 10: Prepare for independent use

Priya is the recovery outcome owner; Jordan provides peer review and backup; Diego owns business-hours evidence/exception intake; Nate supplies technical evidence within the authorized cap; the Head owns prioritization and approval routing. Confirm the customer roster maintainer and receiving operator rather than inventing an assignment.

September 21 receiving demonstration: retrieve a representative case, explain expected status/recipient, update an approved roster entry through the documented process, and route an exception to its owner without coaching. Priya records pass or gap. If access, owner nomination, documentation, technical work, or customer confirmation remains missing, the recovery stays open with a dated next action and explicit support dependency.
Step 11: Synthesize and present

Ephrata's promised relief remains unverified after narrow checks and premature outcome closure. The next technical cause is still unknown. This plan allocates 47 hours to investigation and conditional verification, protects Durant's existing exit obligations, and gives Medford a scoped response. It preserves queue coverage and thirty nonengineering contingency hours while accepting that nine engineering hours may not deliver a complete repair.

Demonstration: show the diagnosis evidence map, then Step 7 and the workbook's account/person totals. Change an input to expose a capacity conflict or coverage gap and restore it. Show a blocked work record with its next action, then the handoff's evidence gates and customer drafts. Close with what is proven by the artifact checks and what still needs live verification.

Submission: ephrata_recovery_package.zip containing the diagnosis, Excel operating plan, and executable handoff at its root. The private repository and its update log preserve each meaningful change: https://github.com/yaseen-bhat/zingage-ephrata-recovery. The complete dated source citations are in both the diagnosis and workbook. No proposed customer outcome is presented as achieved.
